subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or keep steering boundary-based by default?
rationale: Current main implements boundary steering plus partial active-run admission fixes, while the requested pause-or-abort/inject/resume lifecycle changes shared runtime behavior and needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document the current model-boundary behavior as the supported default and use linked work only to ensure messages reach that policy reliably.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after upgrade and channel/runtime compatibility proof.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the replacement PR for the active-run steering path and are the strongest available owner signal for the shared lifecycle tradeoff.
